sections.h2: Where do I pay property tax in Camden County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Camden County Tax Commissioner collects property tax from an office at 200 E 4th Street in Woodbine, the county seat. The mailing address is PO Box 698, Woodbine, GA 31569, the main number is 912-576-3248, and the office is open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Valuation is a separate office. The Board of Tax Assessors, which the Board of Commissioners appoints, answers questions about what your property is worth at 912-576-3241. The tax commissioner's page says plainly that it takes no part in dividing taxes between buyer and seller, and that liability for the tax attaches to the owner.

That last point is worth reading twice if you are selling. The county will not work out a credit for you at closing, so your closing attorney or title company has to prorate the year and request a payoff figure for any balance.

sections.h2: When is the Camden County tax bill due?
sections.html:
Camden bills near the middle of September and the tax is due 60 days after the mail-out date. The notice goes to whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year. If you sold and still receive the bill, forward it to the new owner, and call the office if no bill reaches you by October 15.

The Georgia Department of Revenue publishes a county fact sheet for Camden that gives the statewide default of December 20 and notes that a county can move the date or use installments. Every taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts. Camden's own page is the better guide to its schedule, so confirm the exact date on your bill.

sections.h2: What does it cost to be late in Camden County?
sections.html:
Taxes become delinquent the day after the due date. Interest runs at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent a year, any part of a month counts as a full month, and the minimum interest is $1 (O.C.G.A. 48-5-148). The county's page reproduces a January 2019 monthly rate of 0.7083% as an example, so the current rate will differ.

Penalties are separate. A 5% penalty is added at 120 days late, and again at 240, 360 and 480 days (O.C.G.A. 48-2-44). The penalty does not apply to homestead taxes of $500 or less, or to a new owner who lived outside Georgia, never received a bill and pays within a year of the due date.

  • The week after the due date, the county mails a 30-day notice that a lien is coming.
  • Within a week after that notice period ends, the lien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • The filing cost, which the county lists at $28.50 to $33.50, is added to your tax bill.
  • Once a lien is filed, tax sale proceedings may begin.

sections.h2: How does a Camden County tax sale and redemption work?
sections.html:
A tax lien attaches to the property as of its January 1 valuation (O.C.G.A. 48-2-56), and it ranks ahead of every other lien. On December 31 each year the tax commissioner must issue an execution against delinquent taxpayers (O.C.G.A. 48-3-3), directing the levying officer to collect or to levy and sell.

If a house is sold at a tax sale, the owner can still redeem it. The redemption price is what the buyer paid for the tax deed, plus any taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus 20% of that amount for the first year or part of a year. After the first year the buyer is entitled to an additional 10% for each later year or fraction of a year.

Twelve months after the sale, the buyer may begin the notice process that permanently bars redemption (O.C.G.A. 48-4-45 through 48-4-48). Camden's redemption page notes that the soonest a buyer can gain physical control of the property is one year and forty-five days after the deed. If your house is heading in that direction, selling before the sale date keeps the equity in your hands.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Camden County property value?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date on the Notice of Reassessment. File the appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors, using the contact number 912-576-3241 if you need the form. The state fact sheet adds that the appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the mailing date.

The assessed value is 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and a rise in market value means the assessed value must rise too. The Department of Revenue fact sheet also says refunds for taxes found to be erroneously or illegally assessed can be requested in writing within three years of payment.

  • Returns for property are filed with the county tax office between January 1 and April 1.
  • A homestead application can go in at any time of year, but must arrive by April 1 to count for that year.
  • Failure to apply is treated as a waiver of the exemption.

sections.h2: What is Camden County like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Camden is the southeastern corner of Georgia, bordering Glynn County to the north, Nassau County in Florida to the south, and Charlton and Brantley counties to the west. It spans 782 square miles, and about 22% of that is water, which takes in the St. Marys River and Cumberland Island National Seashore. It is one of Georgia's original counties, created in 1777.

Kingsland is the largest city, St. Marys and Woodbine are the others, and Interstate 95 and U.S. 17 carry most of the traffic. Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, sited on a former Army ocean terminal after the Navy picked Kings Bay in 1976, is the area's anchor, and the county grew quickly through the 1980s because of it. The Gilman Paper mill closed in 2002, and voters overturned the Spaceport Camden land option in a 2022 referendum that the Georgia Supreme Court upheld in February 2023.

faqs.q: Will Camden County prorate the tax for me when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's page says the office has no role in prorating taxes between buyer and seller. Your closing attorney or title company handles the split, and the county's role is to confirm what is owed on the parcel.

faqs.q: What if I never got my Camden County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at 912-576-3248. The county asks anyone who has not received a notice by October 15 to get in touch. Missing a bill does not stop interest from running on an overdue balance.

faqs.q: How soon does a lien follow a missed Camden County due date?
faqs.a: A 30-day lien notice is mailed the week after the due date, and the lien is filed with the Clerk of Superior Court within about a week after that notice period ends. The filing cost, listed at $28.50 to $33.50, goes onto your bill.

faqs.q: Can I stop a Camden County tax sale by paying?
faqs.a: Paying the tax charged against the property releases the lien. After a sale, you can still redeem by paying the buyer's price plus 20% for the first year and 10% more for each later year, until the buyer completes the notice process that bars redemption.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty if my Camden County homestead tax is small?
faqs.a: Not on the late penalty. The 5% penalty does not apply to homestead taxes of $500 or less. Interest still applies to a late balance, at the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, with a $1 minimum.
